findings.claim: Longitude reduction introduces an antimeridian error exceeding the directional metre tolerance, and the high-precision oracle repeats it.
findings.evidence: Production subtracts 2*math.pi before trigonometry. pipeline/tests/test_geometry_aeqd.py:210-219 also constructs its high-precision period from math.pi rather than preserving the input angle or reducing by true 2*pi. Algebraic counterexample, not executed: on Earth, lat0=lat=0, lon0=-math.pi+1e-7 and lon=math.pi-1e-7 describe points about 1.2742 m apart. The rounded-period reduction changes the spherical angle by approximately 2.4492936e-16 rad, shifting x by 1.56e-9 m against an allowance of approximately 1.28e-10 m. Both implementation and oracle share that shift. A stated longitude range does not change the sphere's trigonometric period; use an independent true-sphere oracle and retain the period residual in production reduction.

resolution.reason: Confirmed and fixed. Under a true-sphere oracle the reviewer's case (Earth, lat0 = lat = 0, lon0 = -math.pi + 1e-7, lon = math.pi - 1e-7) moved x by 1.56e-9 m against an allowance of 1.28e-10 m. 96bb648 makes the oracles independent of the module's convention: exact_forward takes each float64 longitude at its exact value with mpmath's pi and no reduction, exact_inverse turns by the true 2 pi, and assert_angles_close turns by 2 * math.pi plus the mpmath residual. It adds the counterexample and eight more antimeridian cases per body, and a test that the inverse returns the in-range float64 nearest the exact longitude on the true circle (76 failed before the fix). df775d3 carries the residual 2.4492935982947064e-16 in the low part of the forward's exact longitude difference, and the inverse forms lam0 + atan2(N, M) exactly and returns the nearest in-range float64 on the true circle, -math.pi or the largest float64 below math.pi in the 2.4e-16 rad gap at the antimeridian. Both directions must change together: with only the forward changed, pixel-centre round trips in Earth windows just east of -pi used up to 1.19 of the allowance against the true sphere (168 of 400 such centres in a scratch search); 7b2d4b6 pins three. Now 0 of 400 fail, peak 0.565 (the longitude floor), and 20,000-example runs of the three property tests pass.

findings.claim: The round-trip property omits the required random window widths and spacings.
findings.evidence: The @given arguments at :761-765 vary only body, centre and pixel indices. Lines 783-785 always select coordinates from window_grid(WINDOW_M, GRID_M), fixed to 5000 m and 90 m by config/run.yaml:21-24. Other grid dimensions at :376-395 only test grid construction, without projection round trips. AC5 explicitly requires generated widths up to 5000 m and spacings. These grids can contain zero or much smaller components, so fixed-grid coverage does not establish the required domain. Add that coverage or obtain an explicit contract amendment addressing its float64 limitations.

resolution.reason: Fixed under the orchestrator decision of 2026-11-14T19:41:28Z (story notes), which amends criterion 5 (1). Random widths and spacings turned the round trip into a continuous-offset round trip in metres, which float64 cannot meet at PRD 7 atol 1e-12 m in about 2% of random grids, and contradicted part (2). Part (1) now covers the two D29 grids the system evaluates: W = 5000 m at 90 m (terrain.analysis_grid_m) and W = 5000 m at 78.125 m (ml.input_m_per_px, 64 px), at random centres on all three bodies and at every pixel centre, with PRD 7 rtol 1e-10 and atol 1e-12 m unchanged. f81b1a9 added the encoder grid, read from the run config, to the parametrised grid round trips and to the Hypothesis round-trip property. 0f6e079 makes the property round-trip every pixel centre of the drawn grid through the module forward at each random centre, and the drawn pixels also through the 40-digit reference forward. Random widths and spacings stay in test_grid_property_at_random_widths_and_spacings, which checks the grid formula only. Checks: uv run pytest pipeline/tests/test_geometry_aeqd.py, 713 passed; make check exit 0. Scratch run, not committed: 10,000 random examples of the property, each over a full grid, passed in 15.6 s.
